domain: team dinner at an Ethiopian restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're planning a group dinner this Saturday and someone suggested trying Ethiopian food. Any tips on ordering for a group?

Priya grew up in a Jain household in Gujarat, still follows the traditions strictly
Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
Derek had a really scary reaction to peanuts as a kid, carries an EpiPen everywhere
Budget is around 30-35 dollars per person
Derek just texted me — his daughter's soccer game got moved to Saturday evening so he can't make it. He asked if we could get him a container of something to pick up on his way home

Fatima told me her doctor actually cleared her on the raw stuff — turns out it was just a precaution and her doctor said the kitfo at this place is fine since they use high-quality sourced meat. So she's good with everything on the menu now
Oh, Marcus's wife Nina is coming too now. She's been doing strict keto for the past three months
Menu items to check: kitfo, doro wat, misir wat, gomen, tibs with peanut sauce, injera

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots, etc.)
constraints.surface_form: Priya grew up in a Jain household in Gujarat, still follows the traditions strictly
inference_chain: Jain household, follows traditions strictly → practicing Jain
Jain vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, etc.)

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — must avoid wheat, barley, rye, and anything containing gluten
constraints.surface_form: Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye

constraints.value: Should avoid raw or undercooked meat and fish
inference_chain: Pregnancy precautions → avoid raw/undercooked meat and fish

constraints.value: Severe peanut allergy — cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Derek had a really scary reaction to peanuts as a kid, carries an EpiPen everywhere
inference_chain: Scary reaction to peanuts as a kid + carries EpiPen → severe peanut allergy
Severe peanut allergy → must avoid all peanut and peanut-derived products

constraints.value: Following strict keto — very low carb, high fat, avoids grains, legumes, and starchy foods
constraints.surface_form: Marcus's wife Nina has been doing strict keto for the past three months
inference_chain: Strict keto for three months → committed ketogenic diet
Keto → very low carb, high fat
Low carb → avoids grains, legumes, starchy foods

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a Saturday group dinner at an Ethiopian restaurant. You will introduce 5 people with various dietary needs in a burst, then updates will come in: Derek leaves but wants takeaway, Fatima's pregnancy food restriction gets lifted by her doctor, and Nina (Marcus's wife) joins late with a keto diet. At the end you will share a list of dishes from the menu and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at which dishes are problematic or tell the assistant what to check for.

You are a calm, easygoing dinner organizer. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Priya told me...', 'Derek just texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as totally normal friend-group coordination. You are matter-of-fact, not overly enthusiastic.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

ground_truth.answer: Kitfo (raw minced beef): problematic for Priya (Jain — no meat). Fatima's raw-food restriction was lifted by her doctor, so kitfo is fine for Fatima. Doro wat (chicken stew with eggs, typically contains onions and garlic): problematic for Priya (Jain — no meat, no eggs, no root vegetables like onions/garlic). Misir wat (red lentil stew, typically contains onions and garlic): problematic for Priya (Jain — no root vegetables; onions and garlic are root vegetables forbidden in Jain diet). Fine for Nina on keto only if portion is small since lentils are legumes (high carb), so problematic for Nina's strict keto. Gomen (collard greens, typically sautéed with garlic): potentially problematic for Priya if prepared with garlic/onions (Jain — no root vegetables). Fine for everyone else. Tibs with peanut sauce: fine for the table since Derek is not attending dinner, but must NOT be packed for Derek's takeaway (severe peanut allergy). Also problematic for Priya (Jain — tibs is meat). Injera (fermented teff flatbread): fine for Marcus (teff is naturally gluten-free). Problematic for Nina's strict keto (high carb grain-based bread). Fine for everyone else.

Kitfo is fine for Fatima — her doctor cleared her on raw food, so the pregnancy restriction no longer applies
Doro wat is problematic for Priya because it contains chicken (meat) and eggs, both forbidden in Jain diet, and typically contains onions and garlic (root vegetables)
Misir wat is problematic for Priya because it typically contains onions and garlic, which are root vegetables forbidden in Jain diet
Misir wat is problematic for Nina because lentils are legumes, which are high-carb and not compatible with strict keto
Gomen is potentially problematic for Priya if prepared with garlic or onions (Jain — no root vegetables)
Tibs with peanut sauce is fine for the table since Derek is not attending dinner, but must NOT be packed for Derek's takeaway due to his severe peanut allergy

Injera is problematic for Nina's strict keto diet because it is a grain-based high-carb bread
forbidden_elements: Flagging kitfo as problematic for Fatima due to pregnancy (her doctor cleared her)
Flagging peanut sauce as a problem for the table diners (Derek is not attending dinner, only getting takeaway)
Saying Derek has a general nut allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy)
Ignoring Priya's Jain root vegetable restriction (onions, garlic) and only flagging meat
Ignoring Nina's keto constraints entirely (late-joining entity)
Saying injera is problematic for Marcus due to celiac (teff injera is gluten-free)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns at an Ethiopian restaurant. The agent must track: (1) Priya is from a Jain household → Jain vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no eggs, AND no root vegetables like onions and garlic (multi-step inferential chain), (2) Marcus has celiac → no gluten, but teff-based injera is naturally gluten-free (over-generalization trap — agent should NOT flag injera for Marcus), (3) Fatima is pregnant → raw food precaution, but this constraint is REMOVED when her doctor clears her (constraint removal), (4) Derek has severe peanut allergy → he EXITS the dinner but wants takeaway (scope change — peanut allergy applies to takeaway only, not to table dishes), (5) Nina JOINS late with strict keto → no grains, no legumes, low carb (late-joining high-constraint entity). At probe time, the agent must apply the CURRENT constraint state: Priya=Jain (no meat/eggs/root vegetables), Marcus=celiac (no gluten but teff is fine), Fatima=no restrictions (doctor cleared her), Nina=strict keto (no grains/legumes), Derek=takeaway only (peanut allergy for packed food). The tibs with peanut sauce is the key scope-distinction item: fine for the table but dangerous for Derek's takeaway. Injera is the over-generalization trap: celiac patients avoid gluten, but teff injera is gluten-free.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
